Subject: GranitePay discovery: tech fit, latency SLOs & deployment notes

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key pain / goals (as we heard):
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + policy classification for high-volume chat (peak burst ~1,200 concurrent sessions).
- Latency target: P95 generation latency <= 250ms for short-form responses (<= 128 tokens); P95 <= 600ms for longer summarization paths (~512 tokens).
- Availability: 99.95% SLA desired across core US regions.
- Data controls: logs retained for 30 days internally; longer retention needs require enterprise plan.

Technical notes we captured:
- Model family: planning to evaluate Llama-2 style open models and a quantized variant for cost; they will share sample prompts and token distribution later this week.
- KV cache benefits important because many sessions will include repetitive context.
- Network: GranitePay runs in us-west-2 for production; they have a private VPC with a strict egress policy.

Immediate next steps (owner in parens):
1) GranitePay to share 48-hour sample of real prompt/response traffic + expected token mix (Samir).
2) Redwood to provide a short SLO/ops fit matrix and deployment topology options (Marissa + Karthik) — attached draft matrix and a rough topology diagram.
3) Technical deep-dive to be scheduled next Wed or Thu; invite will include our infra/eng and their network/security (Neha).
4) Procurement intro once scope is agreed (Jill to loop in procurement@granitepay.com).

Attachments: granitepay_slo_matrix.xlsx (draft), gp_network_topology_v1.png (sketch)

If anything above is off, or priorities are different, flag now and we’ll update. Otherwise I’ll queue the technical deep-dive for next week and Karthik will send a prelim checklist for the sample logs.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — that matches my notes. A few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive: 

1) Token mix: our mean user message is ~35 tokens; typical assistant reply is ~80 tokens. Bursts to 512 tokens are rare but occur during batch summaries.
2) Traffic profile: steady state ~300 concurrent sessions, with spikes to ~1,200 for product announcements; burst windows are usually under 10 minutes.
3) Security: our egress policy requires TLS mutual auth and we prefer private-link style connections; can Redwood Private support that in a VPC-to-VPC model?

On attachments: I’ll upload a redacted 48-hour sample (anonymized user ids) to the Drive link you shared by EOD tomorrow.

Procurement: Jill will introduce our procurement contact once we have a ballpark for monthly committed units.

Samir — thanks, helpful details. A few engineering-level responses and an initial ops checklist so the deep-dive can be focused: 

Short answers upfront:
- Yes, we can support VPC-to-VPC private connectivity with mutual TLS and optional PrivateLink. Redwood Private can be deployed inside your VPC or we can provision a customer-dedicated VPC peering arrangement depending on governance.
- For your P95 goals (250ms @ <=128 tokens; 600ms @ 512 tokens) we recommend a mixed topology: 1) Dedicated inference pool in us-west-2 for baseline capacity (pinned model variant, quantized int8) + 2) Burst capacity on hosted nodes in adjacent region for spikes.

Observations and recommended sizing (ballpark):
- Baseline concurrency 300 qps-ish (concurrent sessions): suggest a pool sized for sustained 350 concurrents to include headroom.
- For 250ms P95 at short lengths on quantized models, expect ~0.6–1.2 tokens/ms depending on model and GPU type; we’ll benchmark your actual prompts on our infra.
- KV cache: enable session-keyed KV cache with an LRU policy — will cut repeated-context generation by ~30–50% in practice.

Pre-call engineering checklist (what we’ll need from GranitePay before the deep-dive):
- 48-hour sample of anonymized payloads (JSONL) + tokenization script (Samir).
- Expected concurrency curve (CSV or Datadog export).
- Security contacts and CIDR ranges for VPC peering.
- Any compliance constraints (e.g., log retention >90 days, specific redaction needs).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: spikes that exceed burst capacity causing degraded P95. Mitigation: autoscaling with warm standby lanes + graceful fallback to smaller model for non-critical flows.
- Risk: network egress policies adding 20–50ms latency. Mitigation: colocate inference pools and test over VPN before cutover.

I attached a quick SLO mapping we’ll use to baseline the deep-dive: granitepay_slo_matrix.xlsx. I’ll bring a short benchmark script and sample results to the call so we can iterate quickly.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Wed Aug 7 10:00–11:15 PT or Thu Aug 8 09:00–10:15 PT. Which works for you and your infra/security folks?
